_comment: Edit this file, not the code. Bands: 1 cheap workhorse, 2 mid, 3 deep. Ladders are ordered preferences; the router filters by live quota and then prefers the eligible candidate whose quota bucket resets soonest (spend what expires first).

claude._note: Claude Code publishes no quota API. Leave null and Claude stays escalation-only (band 3). Set a token budget to let it take ordinary work.

openrouter._note: 1000/day applies with 10 USD or more of lifetime credit, otherwise 50/day. Counted locally in state.json.

_comment_free: opencode_zen entries here are the -free models, served to the OpenCode client without touching the Go subscription buckets. Slower than the paid cheap band, so the ladder keeps them last: overflow capacity, not the default.
_comment_cache: Seconds a quota reading stays usable for routing. A dispatch takes minutes, so a reading a minute old is the same reading. `rightsize probe` and `route --fresh` always re-read.

launchers._doc: How a decision becomes a command. Each launcher maps a provider to a template, with `default` covering the rest. Fields: {provider} {agent} {model} {model_ref} {effort} {band} {spec} {spec_path}. Adding a launcher is config, not code: see docs/ADAPTERS.md.

orca.default:
orca orchestration worker-start --spec {spec} --worktree current --agent {agent} --json
# then inside that terminal: opencode -m {model_ref}
